## Introduction {#introduction}

I'm preparing for a hands-on workshop where we'll build a **Photo-to-Video AI App** from scratch. Before diving into code, I wanted to understand the architecture deeply. This post documents my research and preparation.

::: {.callout-note}
## What We're Building
A web app where users:

1. Paste a product URL
2. App scrapes images & product context automatically
3. AI generates short promo videos using Google Veo
4. Users can sign in with Google and save videos to Drive
:::

## The Tech Stack {#tech-stack}

| Component | Technology | Purpose |
|-----------|------------|---------|
| Frontend | Next.js | React-based UI with App Router |
| Backend | Supabase | Database, Auth, Edge Functions |
| AI Video | Google Veo 3.1 | Image-to-video generation |
| Deployment | Vercel | Serverless hosting |
| Development | Google Antigravity | AI-assisted development |
| Auth | Google OAuth | Sign-in + Drive access |

## Chapter 1: Understanding Google Veo 3.1 {#chapter-1}

Google Veo 3.1 is the star of this application. It generates high-fidelity 8-second videos from images and text prompts.

### Key Capabilities

- **Portrait videos**: Choose between 16:9 and 9:16 aspect ratios
- **Video extension**: Extend previously generated videos
- **Frame-specific generation**: Specify first and/or last frames
- **Image-based direction**: Use up to 3 reference images
- **Native audio**: Generates synchronized sound effects and conversations

### API Structure

The Veo API uses a **long-running operations** pattern:

```
Endpoint: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/veo-3.1-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
Method: POST
Auth: x-goog-api-key header
```

### Required Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| `prompt` | string | Text description (supports audio cues) |
| `image` | Image object | Initial frame for animation |
| `aspectRatio` | string | "16:9" (default) or "9:16" |
| `resolution` | string | "720p", "1080p", or "4k" |
| `durationSeconds` | string | "4", "6", or "8" |

### Python Example

```python
import time
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client()

# Generate video from an image
operation = client.models.generate_videos(
    model="veo-3.1-generate-preview",
    prompt="A sleek product rotating slowly with soft lighting",
    image=product_image,
    config=types.GenerateVideosConfig(
        aspect_ratio="16:9",
        resolution="1080p",
        duration_seconds="8"
    )
)

# Poll for completion (can take up to 6 minutes)
while not operation.done:
    time.sleep(10)
    operation = client.operations.get(operation)

# Get the generated video
video = operation.result.generated_videos[0]
```

### JavaScript/Node.js Example

```javascript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY });

let operation = await ai.models.generateVideos({
    model: "veo-3.1-generate-preview",
    prompt: "Product showcase with dynamic camera movement",
    image: imageData,
    config: {
        aspectRatio: "16:9",
        resolution: "1080p"
    }
});

// Poll until done
while (!operation.done) {
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10000));
    operation = await ai.operations.getVideosOperation({ operation });
}

const videoUrl = operation.result.generatedVideos[0].video.uri;
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Veo Limitations to Know

- **Latency**: 11 seconds minimum, up to 6 minutes during peak
- **Video retention**: Generated videos stored for **2 days only**
- **Watermarking**: All videos watermarked with SynthID
- **Resolution for extension**: Video extension limited to 720p
- **Reference images**: Maximum 3 images, 16:9 aspect ratio only
- **Pricing**: $0.75 per second of video output (paid tier required)
:::

## Chapter 2: Web Scraping Product Pages {#chapter-2}

To extract product images and context from URLs, we have two main options:

### Playwright vs Puppeteer

| Feature | Playwright | Puppeteer |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| Browser Support | Chromium, Firefox, WebKit | Chromium (limited Firefox) |
| Success Rate | ~96% on 1000+ pages | ~75% after 500 pages |
| Anti-bot evasion | Good, needs configuration | Better with stealth plugins |
| Best for | Dynamic/high-volume | Stable content, lightweight |

### Basic Scraping Pattern

```javascript
import { chromium } from 'playwright';

async function scrapeProductPage(url) {
    const browser = await chromium.launch();
    const page = await browser.newPage();

    await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });

    // Extract product images
    const images = await page.$$eval('img', imgs =>
        imgs.map(img => ({
            src: img.src,
            alt: img.alt
        })).filter(img =>
            img.src.includes('product') ||
            img.alt.toLowerCase().includes('product')
        )
    );

    // Extract product title
    const title = await page.$eval('h1', el => el.textContent);

    // Extract description
    const description = await page.$eval(
        '[class*="description"], [id*="description"]',
        el => el.textContent
    ).catch(() => '');

    await browser.close();

    return { images, title, description };
}
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Anti-Bot Considerations

Modern e-commerce sites use sophisticated detection. For production:

- Use `puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth`
- Randomize user agents and fingerprints
- Add realistic delays between actions
- Consider using a proxy service for scale
:::

## Chapter 3: Supabase as Your Backend {#chapter-3}

Supabase provides everything we need: database, authentication, and edge functions.

### Why Supabase for AI Apps?

- **Vector storage**: Built-in pgvector for embeddings
- **Edge Functions**: Run AI logic close to users
- **Real-time**: Live updates for video generation status
- **Auth**: Built-in Google OAuth integration

### Database Schema for Video Generation

```sql
-- Users table (managed by Supabase Auth)
-- Videos table
CREATE TABLE videos (
    id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    product_url TEXT NOT NULL,
    product_title TEXT,
    product_images JSONB,
    video_url TEXT,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending, generating, completed, failed
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Enable Row Level Security
ALTER TABLE videos ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Users can only see their own videos
CREATE POLICY "Users can view own videos"
    ON videos FOR SELECT
    USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
```

### Edge Function for Video Generation

```typescript
// supabase/functions/generate-video/index.ts
import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts"
import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from "@google/generative-ai"

serve(async (req) => {
    const { imageUrl, prompt } = await req.json()

    const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI(Deno.env.get("GEMINI_API_KEY")!)

    // Start video generation
    const operation = await genAI.models.generateVideos({
        model: "veo-3.1-generate-preview",
        prompt,
        image: { uri: imageUrl }
    })

    return new Response(JSON.stringify({
        operationId: operation.name
    }))
})
```

## Chapter 4: Google OAuth Done Right {#chapter-4}

The workshop emphasizes **incremental permissions** - a best practice that improves user trust.

### The Principle

Don't ask for all permissions upfront. Instead:

1. **Sign-in**: Request basic profile only (`openid`, `email`, `profile`)
2. **When saving to Drive**: Request `drive.file` scope
3. **When picking folders**: Use Google Picker API

### Implementation Pattern

```javascript
// Initial sign-in - minimal scopes
const authorizationUrl = oauth2Client.generateAuthUrl({
    access_type: 'offline',
    scope: ['openid', 'email', 'profile'],
    include_granted_scopes: true  // Enable incremental auth
});

// Later, when user wants to save to Drive
const driveAuthUrl = oauth2Client.generateAuthUrl({
    access_type: 'offline',
    scope: ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file'],
    include_granted_scopes: true
});
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why `drive.file` Instead of Full Drive Access?

The `drive.file` scope is **non-sensitive** and:

- Only accesses files your app creates or user explicitly selects
- Streamlines Google verification process
- Builds user trust
- Works perfectly with Google Picker API
:::

### Google Picker Integration

```javascript
// Load the Google Picker API
function loadPicker() {
    gapi.load('picker', { callback: createPicker });
}

function createPicker() {
    const picker = new google.picker.PickerBuilder()
        .addView(google.picker.ViewId.FOLDERS)
        .setOAuthToken(accessToken)
        .setCallback(pickerCallback)
        .build();
    picker.setVisible(true);
}

function pickerCallback(data) {
    if (data.action === google.picker.Action.PICKED) {
        const folderId = data.docs[0].id;
        // Save video to this folder
    }
}
```

## Chapter 5: Deploying on Vercel {#chapter-5}

Vercel makes deployment straightforward, but there are AI-specific considerations.

### Environment Variables Setup

```bash
# .env.local (never commit this!)
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key
SUPABASE_URL=https://yourproject.supabase.co
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_anon_key
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your_oauth_client_id
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your_oauth_client_secret
```

On Vercel:
1. Go to Settings > Environment Variables
2. Add each variable for Production/Preview/Development
3. Use `vercel env pull .env.local` to sync locally

### Function Duration for AI

Video generation can take minutes. Configure longer timeouts:

```typescript
// app/api/generate-video/route.ts
export const maxDuration = 60; // seconds (max on Hobby tier)

export async function POST(req: Request) {
    // Video generation logic
}
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Rate Limiting is Essential

AI APIs are expensive. Implement rate limiting:

```typescript
import { Ratelimit } from "@upstash/ratelimit";

const ratelimit = new Ratelimit({
    redis: Redis.fromEnv(),
    limiter: Ratelimit.slidingWindow(5, "1 h"), // 5 requests per hour
});
```
:::

## Chapter 6: Google Antigravity for Development {#chapter-6}

The workshop uses **Google Antigravity**, an AI-powered development platform.

### What Makes It Different

- **Agent-first**: AI agents autonomously plan, execute, and verify tasks
- **Two interfaces**:
  - Editor View (traditional IDE with AI completions)
  - Manager Surface (spawn and observe multiple agents)
- **Artifacts**: Visual proof of work (screenshots, recordings, plans)
- **Knowledge base**: Agents retain context for better future performance

### Supported Models

- Gemini 3 Pro (default)
- Claude Sonnet 4.5
- GPT-OSS

### Getting Started

1. Download from `antigravity.google/download`
2. Available for macOS, Windows, Linux
3. Free during public preview

## The Architecture Diagram {#architecture}

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         USER BROWSER                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Paste URL  │  2. View Status  │  3. Download/Save to Drive  │
└────────┬───────┴────────┬─────────┴──────────┬──────────────────┘
         │                │                    │
         ▼                ▼                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    NEXT.JS ON VERCEL                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  /api/scrape      │  /api/generate   │  /api/save-to-drive      │
│  Playwright       │  Veo API call    │  Google Drive API        │
└────────┬──────────┴────────┬─────────┴──────────┬───────────────┘
         │                   │                    │
         ▼                   ▼                    ▼
┌─────────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────┐
│   SUPABASE      │  │  GOOGLE VEO   │  │    GOOGLE DRIVE        │
│   - PostgreSQL  │  │  3.1 API      │  │    (User's account)    │
│   - Auth        │  │               │  │                        │
│   - Storage     │  │  $0.75/sec    │  │    OAuth + Picker      │
└─────────────────┘  └───────────────┘  └────────────────────────┘
```
